doc.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]

title: More Stash records and years working with Bucky
summary: Follow-up Stash records and playing everywhere with his father from 1980 to 1989.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I might be rambling you know. I never am allowed to talk this much. And still I do. But it was one of those things. I mean this song became a sort of little hit, this “I Like Jersey Best” thing and then like a year later Stash said, “let’s make another record.” So I made another record and Dave McKenna was in town. I said, “well let’s get McKenna, and we’ll get Butch Miles and Jerry Bruno played bass, and we did half with them and my dad, some more Nat King Cole things “This Will Make You Laugh,” “Hit That Jive Jack,” and then with my friend Steve Ferrera on drums and Gary Haase on bass, we did “Haven’t We Met,” we made like a little sort of rock record of “Racing With the Moon” with a little backbeat, and did some more original songs and that came out. And that’s all been re-released sort of on CDs along the way. And I made one more for Stash. And so the records got reviewed and I was just working with my dad from 1980 to 1989 we worked everywhere and anywhere — house parties, concerts, we would play clubs out in Jersey, The Cornerstone out in New Jersey in Metuchen and nobody would listen, everybody would be talking away you know, and we’d sit and play for two hours, just talking to each other. “Okay what do you want to play, okay,” boom.
Yeah. You’re getting paid to rehearse.
